question: Should OpenClaw core own a durable plugin allow-always approval store keyed by plugin/tool/scope, and may Skill Workshop opt into that store for lifecycle actions?
rationale: Durable allow-always reuse suppresses future approval prompts and becomes a plugin-facing API/security contract; automation cannot decide the permanent trust boundary, retention, revocation, or Skill Workshop authority model.

options.title: Fix durable scope before merge
options.body: Require a stable owner id, non-sensitive request-visible scope, current-main rebase, and second-call reuse proof before accepting the API.

options.title: Split Skill Workshop opt-in out
options.body: Land only the generic mechanism after API review and keep Skill Workshop on allow-once/deny until its lifecycle authority model is settled.

options.title: Accept the expanded API explicitly
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally accept the new durable plugin approval contract after documenting scope, security expectations, and upgrade behavior.

recommendation.title: Fix durable scope before merge
recommendation.body: Require a stable owner id, non-sensitive request-visible scope, current-main rebase, and second-call reuse proof before accepting the API.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main ownership touches the affected approval and Skill Workshop paths, making this the best available routing candidate for the cross-boundary decision.
